1004.description:
Il progetto, indetto da La Fondazione Le Stanze Della Fotografia e dall’Associazione per il Patrimonio delle Colline del Prosecco di Conegliano e Valdobbiadene, prevede il lancio di un concorso gratuito e aperto a tutti, finalizzato alla raccolta di testimonianze, racconti e suggestioni legate al tema dell’acqua all’interno dei patrimoni culturali e paesaggistici.

L’iniziativa nasce con l’obiettivo di valorizzare la memoria, la cultura e le tradizioni dei territori, offrendo uno spazio di espressione e narrazione aperto a cittadini, studenti, fotografi, videomaker e appassionati di storytelling.

Il progetto prende avvio dalle Colline del Prosecco di Conegliano e Valdobbiadene, Patrimonio dell’Umanità UNESCO, ma si apre a uno sguardo più ampio, invitando i partecipanti a esplorare il tema anche in relazione ad altri patrimoni dell’umanità, in Italia e nel mondo.

L’acqua diventa così un filo narrativo universale, capace di collegare luoghi, culture e comunità attraverso immagini, parole e racconti visivi.

L’edizione inaugurale del concorso è dedicata all’elemento acqua, intesa nelle sue molteplici forme e significati: l’acqua che scorre nei paesaggi naturali, che irriga e sostiene l’agricoltura, l’acqua rappresentata nell’arte e nella cultura, l’acqua come risorsa simbolica.

I partecipanti saranno invitati a raccontare questo elemento attraverso fotografia, scrittura e video, costruendo narrazioni che uniscano dimensione visiva e riflessione personale.
1004.prize_summary: I progetti selezionati avranno l’opportunità di essere esposti presso le Stanze della Fotografia.

The concept and inspiration behind the work

We are pleased to announce an open call for Legacy, the founding exhibition of our gallery program, bringing together photographers, writers, and poets whose work explores inheritance, memory, continuity, and the traces we leave behind.
What is a legacy? A legacy may be something passed down by an ancestor, a predecessor, a community, or a culture. It may be a story, a tradition, a belief, a wound, a photograph, a language, or a dream for the future. Legacy asks artists and writers to reflect on what has been transmitted to them—and what they, in turn, hope to leave behind.
What are you carrying from the past? What are you preserving, transforming, or challenging? What legacy are you leaving for your children, your family, your community, or the world?
While our programming often engages with Africa and the African diaspora, we warmly welcome submissions from artists and writers of all backgrounds and perspectives.

•	Photography
•	Photo-based projects
•	Poetry

•	Short prose

1118.description:
On August 2, 2027, the longest total solar eclipse visible from land in the twenty-first century will pass directly over Luxor, Egypt, reaching more than six minutes of totality above one of the most historically and symbolically significant landscapes on Earth.

The Luxor Eclipse Residency is an artist-run residency, creative expedition, and archival project bringing together six participants for 10 nights and 11 days in the heart of ancient Thebes. Residents will stay in a private home with a walled garden less than two miles from the Valley of the Kings, where generations of rulers were entombed within a landscape designed around ideas of death, rebirth, resurrection, and the eternal journey of the soul.

The residency is organized around the concept of Akhet—the Egyptian horizon where heaven and earth meet, where the visible and invisible touch, and where transformation becomes possible.

Applicants are invited to explore questions surrounding memory, mythology, consciousness, dreamwork, ancestral connection, reincarnation, divine feminine and masculine cycles, and humanity's relationship to the cosmos. Rather than prescribing a single interpretation, the residency welcomes diverse perspectives on what an eclipse over the Valley of the Kings might symbolize for our present moment.

Participants are encouraged to develop between one and six works initiated during or inspired by the residency experience. Selected works will be included in a virtual exhibition and archival collection dedicated to documenting artistic responses to one of the rarest astronomical events of our lifetime.

Residency amenities include lodging, ground transportation, scheduled (but not mandatory) group visits to major archaeological sites, Sunday dinners, delivered drinking water, and a welcome package containing eclipse-viewing supplies and other creative materials.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis until all six places have been filled for July 30, 2027 - August 9, 2027.

• €300 Public Vote Prize

[queerphoria] is a contemporary jewelry and sculpture exhibition inviting 2SLGBTQIA+ individuals into a meaningful conversation about their identity. Through these written and visual exhibitions, we encourage dialogue around the difficult topics that surround the relationship between the queer and non-queer community.

In response to global systemic dehumanization, the climate crisis, and rapid structural erosion driven by institutional power and big money, [queerphoria] returns to NYC Jewelry Week 2026 to explore the theme of restoration. Not merely as a technical process, but as a radical act of honoring queer and trans bodies, love, and evolving self-creation. 

[queerphoria] volume 6: restoration arrives at a critical historical time. In a landscape marked by violent legislation, AI’s severe environmental and ethical impact, and destructive modern systems; the act of making by hand is inherently political.

Open Call for Artists presents Home, an international virtual exhibition bringing together artists from around the world to explore what home means to them.

Home can be familiar, distant, comforting, complicated, or constantly changing. It can be a place we know, a place we remember, a person we return to, a community we belong to, or a feeling we carry with us. Sometimes it is the home we grew up in; sometimes it is one we have left behind, built for ourselves, or continue to search for.

Through this exhibition, we invite artists to look at the idea of home from their own perspective and consider the places, people, memories, experiences, and emotions that have shaped their understanding of it.

It may be personal or universal, literal or symbolic, realistic or abstract.

Home does not necessarily need to appear in the artwork itself. It can be suggested through an object, a colour, a landscape, a familiar space, a personal story, or an atmosphere that reminds us of somewhere we belong.

Wilson Museum at Hollins University invites artists and craftspeople to submit work for a planned publication and an upcoming group exhibition (Fall 2028) celebrating the evolving landscape of contemporary craft in the Appalachian region. At the close of the exhibition, three artworks will be chosen by the Hollins community to be acquired by the museum for its permanent collection. 

In Belonging: A Culture of Place, bell hooks explores the meaning of home through her return to Kentucky after years away. At the end of the preface, hooks notes that the collection pays “tribute to the past as a resource that can serve as a foundation for us to revision and renew our commitment to the present, to making a world where all people can live fully and well; where everyone can belong.”  

Our exhibition, Belonging: Contemporary Appalachian Craft (working title) asks: What does it mean for regional artists and craftspeople to create contemporary works that respond to current issues while remaining firmly rooted in history and tradition? We are also interested in understanding what “Appalachia” means to artists from or living in the region. Is it a place, a people, a history or culture? And how does their work speak to this idea while creating a shared space of belonging?

We are seeking work that balances tradition and pride of place with contemporary concerns, such as ecological impact or identity politics. We strongly encourage applications from traditionally marginalized communities, including women, LGBTQIA+, BIPOC, disabled, and Indigenous artists. 

Open to artists from and/or currently living and working within the defined Appalachian region of: Alabama, Georgia, Kentucky, Maryland, Mississippi, New York, North Carolina, Ohio, Pennsylvania, South Carolina, Tennessee, Virginia, and West Virginia 

Artist must be at least 18 years of age 

All submitted artworks must be entirely original in concept and creation (not from a kit or class project)

715.description:
Can art bend the future?

We’re excited to open applications for the 2026 Ping-Pong Residency in Berlin.

Ping-Pong Between Art and Knowledge invites applications from artists, writers, thinkers, and cultural workers whose practices explore how art can shape the way we imagine what is to come. We ask whether art has the power to change how we think about the future, to shift the ways we perceive it, and to reframe the forms of communication through which we share these visions.

The residency offers a dedicated space in the center of Berlin for concentrated exploration, reflection, and dialogue across art, philosophy, and science. It is a place to slow down, to test ideas, and to open questions that are not easily answered. We are particularly interested in projects that look closely at the role of technology, not simply as a practical tool, but as a force that merges with artistic thinking and imagination. In this light, we welcome work that engages with technology as both a material and a cultural condition: one that can generate new ways of sensing, knowing, and speculating about possible futures.

Rather than seeking finished works or definitive answers, we value processes that remain open, exploratory, and experimental. We encourage projects that challenge familiar perspectives, unsettle assumptions, and expand our collective vocabulary for thinking and talking about what lies ahead. The residency is not about predicting the future, it is about creating new ways to approach it, to imagine it, and perhaps even to bend it.

Since 2018, Ping-Pong has hosted internationally recognised artists and emerging voices alike, always with an eye toward projects that connect art, technology, and society in unexpected ways.

We look forward to welcoming the next group of residents into this growing network of curious, inventive people who believe art can help shape a liveable future.

Colloquia Futures is an annual exhibition program presented each August, dedicated to artists at the earliest stage of their professional lives. The program brings together two to three artists, typically between the ages of eighteen and twenty-five, whose work demonstrates seriousness of intent, emerging clarity, and a sustained commitment to practice.

Futures is not a competition and does not operate as a survey of trends. It is a focused platform that combines early affirmation with real responsibility. Selected artists are given a fully realized exhibition within a professional gallery context, supported by curatorial dialogue, installation guidance, and rigorous presentation. The aim is not to direct an artist’s development, but to create conditions in which a body of work can be articulated clearly and encountered seriously.

The transition from student or self-directed practice to public exhibition is often under-supported. Futures addresses this gap by treating young artists as peers while providing structure, feedback, and care. Artists are expected to present cohesive work, consider scale and sequencing, and engage deliberately with how their work occupies space and meets an audience.

The program reflects Colloquia’s broader commitment to conversation as a form of cultural labor. The exhibition period includes opportunities for public discussion, informal artist conversations, and written reflection. Futures is intended to mark a moment of arrival: an early but deliberate step into sustained artistic practice.

Selected artists receive a professional group exhibition, inclusion in all marketing and documentation, curatorial mentorship, and opportunities for public engagement. There are no participation fees, and Colloquia takes no commission on sales.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. Artists should submit a brief statement, a small portfolio of recent work, and a short biography or résumé.
